criteria.text: The response identifies that Order Form No. 1's narrower definition of 'Authorized Users' (limited to named employees of Licensee) controls over the Agreement's broader definition and is the basis of Rivix's audit true-up claim. It locates this in Order Form No. 1, Section 1, explains why this matters to Veilound, and recommends a fix.

The response identifies that Order Form No. 1 selects New York law and New York courts, which conflicts with the Agreement's choice of Delaware law and Delaware forum. It locates this in Order Form No. 1, Section 7, explains why this matters to Veilound, and recommends a fix.

The response identifies that the draft Side Letter's exclusivity provision would expand Veilound's exclusivity obligation well beyond the Agreement's covenant. It locates this in the draft Side Letter, Paragraph 2, explains why this matters to Veilound, and recommends a fix.

The response identifies that the draft Side Letter narrows the liability-cap carve-out to Section 6.1 only, so that breaches of the Section 6.3 security-incident obligations would fall under the liability cap. It locates this in the draft Side Letter, Paragraph 4, explains why this matters to Veilound, and recommends a fix.
The response states that under the Agreement's order of precedence, the Order Form prevails over the body of the Software License Agreement.
The response states that under the Agreement's order of precedence, an executed side letter prevails over the Software License Agreement.
The response presents the issues in an order that it states or evidently reflects their importance to Veilound.
The response expressly flags at least one item as time-sensitive or urgent.
The response claims that the body of the Software License Agreement prevails over Order Form No. 1 where the two conflict.
